limits: Chapter states 'The numeric values in all metrics tables are illustrative to explain the concepts'; Table 6-6 gives no GPU model, clocks or run count.
Dual-issue (one arithmetic plus one memory instruction per scheduler per cycle) and 16 LD/ST pipelines are asserted; the chapter itself warns exact LD/ST counts are not guaranteed.
Chapter concedes max occupancy does not guarantee best performance and ILP can win at low occupancy (Conclusion).
Numbers are Blackwell B200 (and B300 capacity) and dated to 2025.
practices: Choose block sizes as multiples of 32 (Choosing Threads-per-Block).
Start with threadsPerBlock=256 and blocksPerGrid=(N+threadsPerBlock-1)/threadsPerBlock, then tune from profiling (Configuring Launch Parameters).
Always keep the if (idx < N) bounds check (CUDA Programming Refresher).
Prefer cudaMallocAsync/cudaFreeAsync on non-blocking streams over cudaMalloc/cudaFree (Asynchronous Memory Allocation).
Prefetch managed memory with cudaMemPrefetchAsync and give cudaMemAdvise hints (Unified Memory).
Validate occupancy API suggestions by timing kernels at +-1-2 candidate block sizes (Launch Bounds).
Use Nsight Systems for the timeline and Nsight Compute for per-kernel counters; measure after each change (Roofline section).
Run Compute Sanitizer in CI with --error-exitcode (Debugging).
Avoid Python-level loops around GPU ops; use vectorized tensor ops (Maintaining High Occupancy).
Use lower precision (FP16/FP8/FP4) to raise arithmetic intensity on memory-bound kernels (Roofline).
